rationale: Sierra Reads EP. 1 — 'The Inventory.' v3 (writer-agent draft). Sierra calmly enumerates how 'decentered' he is by listing every aspirational item in her apartment, each one secretly bought because of him. The list (Le Creuset, Stanley in sage, Range Rover lease, Wagyu in the freezer, Erewhon membership) is a tight trad-lane brand-cluster the audience instantly recognizes — they see themselves in the items. 'He does not live here. Anymore.' is the rug-pull that retroactively recontextualizes every item as bought-for-him. Catherine Cohen inventory shape, fully committed character. The visual (P37 cafe chin-in-hand cream blazer) reads composed; the words betray her. That's the whole bit.

script_chunks.text: THE LE CREUSET WAS FOR ME.
THE STANLEY IN SAGE — FOR ME.
THE RANGE ROVER LEASE — FOR ME.
THE WAGYU IN THE FREEZER — FOR ME.

voiceover_text: I have fully decentered him. The Le Creuset? For me. The Stanley in sage? For me. The Range Rover lease? For me. The Wagyu in the freezer? For me. The Erewhon membership? For me. He does not live here. Anymore.
caption: decentering him so hard I bought a $90k SUV to drive myself to therapy. ™ The Le Creuset was for me.
tag_line: He does not live here. Anymore.
comedic_devices_used: Catherine-Cohen inventory shape — flat declarative list, dry conviction
trad-lane brand cluster (Le Creuset / Stanley sage / Range Rover / Wagyu / Erewhon) — instant audience recognition
rug-pull button: 'Anymore.' retroactively recontextualizes every line
character-in-denial — she's not joking ABOUT the lie, she's IN the lie
specific receipts > abstractions — each brand is screenshot-able

iteration_history.v0: 'Cool. I've been single 18 months. He's decentered. Now what.' — generic deadpan-shrug, no specifics. Lazy.
iteration_history.v1: Sponsor-read parody (use code 'his loss' for 15% off Decentered.™). Clever structure, AI-feeling, no character.
iteration_history.v2: The Inventory v1 — generic version (Instagram story 16 times this morning). Better mechanic, but no brand cluster, no rug-pull at the end.
iteration_history.v3_current: Inventory v3 from senior comedy-writer agent. Brand-cluster (Le Creuset / Stanley / Range Rover / Wagyu / Erewhon) + 'Anymore.' rug-pull. Catherine-Cohen-coded.

editor_note_for_renderer: Brielle should read the brand names with fake-confident dryness — slight 'of course' lift on each, like she's listing her own receipts. The word 'Anymore' should be a separate beat, almost reluctant, like she let it slip.
